rows.item: Exchange of own CNY principal for USD
rows.rule: No reviewed instrument imposes a tax merely on converting or remitting own principal. Tax attaches to income/gain events.
Statutory progressive rates apply to taxable comprehensive income; residence and source rules matter.
Generally 20% of the balance after original value and reasonable expenses, not 20% of gross principal.
Temporarily exempt under the published Caishui [2008] No.132 notice; do not generalise to every product or US tax.

rows.item: Basic pension / retirement pay under uniform state provisions
rows.rule: Exempt under the IIT law; other retirement income is not automatically exempt.
IIT law requires filing before cancellation of household registration; this is not a transfer tax rate.
US citizens generally report worldwide income regardless of where funds sit.
Qualifying foreign income tax on the same income may be credited subject to limitations; no credit on excluded income.
Aggregate foreign financial accounts above USD 10,000 at any time in the calendar year trigger FinCEN Form 114 for US persons.
Thresholds depend on residence/filing status: US unmarried >50,000 year-end/75,000 any time; qualifying abroad unmarried >200,000/300,000; joint thresholds double.
Above USD 100,000 from a nonresident alien individual/foreign estate can require Form 3520 reporting.
Publication 525 tip: personal FX gain not included unless more than USD 200; above that report as capital gain. Precise application needs manual confirmation.
1% applies to certain remittance transfers after 2025 funded with cash/money order/cashier’s check/similar physical instrument; not a blanket tax on money leaving China.
More than USD 10,000 in covered instruments transported into/out of the US must be reported on FinCEN Form 105; reporting is not a tax.
